nodes.name: Laplacian Matrix
nodes.statement: For weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$, the Laplacian $L_G$ is defined by $L_G(u,v) = -w_{(u,v)}$ if $u \neq v$ and $L_G(u,u) = \sum_z w_{(u,z)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Laplacian of a weighted graph: off-diagonals are negative edge weights; diagonals are sums of incident weights.

nodes.name: Laplacian Quadratic Form
nodes.statement: $x^T L_G x = \sum_{(u,v) \in E} w_{(u,v)} (x(u) - x(v))^2$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}^V$.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-Spectral Approximation
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{G}$ is a $\sigma$-spectral approximation of $G$ if $\frac{1}{\sigma} x^T L_{\widetilde{G}} x \leq x^T L_G x \leq \sigma x^T L_{\widetilde{G}} x$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sparsifier whose Laplacian quadratic form sandwiches that of the original within factor sigma on every vector.

nodes.name: Loewner Order $\preceq$ on Graphs
nodes.statement: Write $A \preceq B$ if $x^T A x \leq x^T B x$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^V$. Overload: $G \preceq \widetilde{G}$ means $L_G \preceq L_{\widetilde{G}}$.

nodes.name: Graph Addition $G + H$
nodes.statement: $G + H$ denotes the graph whose Laplacian is $L_G + L_H$; equivalently, edge weights of corresponding edges sum.

nodes.name: Conductance of a Set
nodes.statement: $\Phi_G(S) \defeq \frac{|E(S, V-S)|}{\min(\mathrm{vol}(S), \mathrm{vol}(V-S))}$, where $\mathrm{vol}(S) = \sum_{i \in S} d_i$.

nodes.name: Normalized Laplacian
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}_G = D^{-1/2} L_G D^{-1/2}$, where $D$ is the diagonal degree matrix.

nodes.name: Induced-Subgraph Conductance $\Phi_B(S)$ and $G\{B\}$
nodes.statement: $\Phi_B(S) \defeq \frac{|E(S,B-S)|}{\min(\mathrm{vol}(S), \mathrm{vol}(B-S))}$ with volume measured by degrees in $G$. $G\{B\}$ adds self-loops to $G(B)$ so each vertex's degree equals its degree in $G$.

nodes.name: $\phi$-Decomposition
nodes.statement: A partition $(A_1,\dots,A_k)$ of $V$ such that $\Phi_{A_i} \geq \phi$ for every $i$.

nodes.name: $\lambda$-Spectral Decomposition
nodes.statement: Partition $(A_1,\dots,A_k)$ of $V$ such that $\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_{G(A_i)}) \geq \lambda$ for every $i$.

nodes.name: Boundary of Decomposition $\partial(A_1,\dots,A_k)$
nodes.statement: $\partial(A_1,\dots,A_k) = E \cap \bigcup_{i \neq j}(A_i \times A_j)$, the edges between different parts.

nodes.name: Contraction and Pullback
nodes.statement: Given partition map $\pi: V \to \{1,\dots,k\}$, the contraction has edge weights $z(i,j) = \sum_{(u,v): \pi(u)=i, \pi(v)=j} w(u,v)$. A pullback of $\widetilde{H}$ assigns each edge of $\widetilde{H}$ to one corresponding original edge $(u,v)$ with $\pi(u)=i, \pi(v)=j$.

nodes.name: Edge and Vertex Blow-Up
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}(e) = \widetilde{w}_e / w_e$ if $e \in \widetilde{E}$, else $0$. $\mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}(v) = \frac{1}{d_v}\sum_{(u,v)\in E} \mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}((u,v))$.

nodes.name: Relative Condition Number $\kappa(G,\widetilde{G})$
nodes.statement: $\kappa(G,\widetilde{G}) \defeq (\max_x x^T L_G x / x^T L_{\widetilde{G}} x) / (\min_x x^T L_G x / x^T L_{\widetilde{G}} x)$.

nodes.name: Cheeger's Inequality
nodes.statement: $2 \Phi_G \geq \lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_G) \geq \Phi_G^2/2$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with normalized Laplacian $\mathcal{L}_G$

nodes.name: Sampling High-Conductance Graphs
nodes.statement: If $G$ is unweighted with $\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_G) \geq \lambda$, then $\widetilde{G}$ produced by $\sample$ on a subset $S$ is, with probability $\geq 1-p$, a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $G$ with at most $\frac{288 \max(\log_2(3/p), \log_2 n)^2}{(\epsilon\lambda)^2}|S|$ sampled edges.
conclusions: With prob. $\geq 1-p$: (S.1) $\widetilde{G} = (V, \widetilde{F} \cup H)$ is a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $G$

nodes.name: Norm-to-Approximation Lemma
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_2(D^{-1/2} L D^{-1/2}) \geq \lambda$ and $\|D^{-1/2}(L-\widetilde{L})D^{-1/2}\| \leq \epsilon$, then $\widetilde{G}$ is a $\sigma$-approximation of $G$ with $\sigma = \lambda/(\lambda - \epsilon)$.
assumptions: $L$ Laplacian of connected $G$, $\widetilde{L}$ Laplacian of $\widetilde{G}$, $D$ diagonal degrees

nodes.name: Random Subgraph (norm bound)
nodes.statement: For all even $k$: $\Pr[\|D^{-1/2}(\widetilde{A}-A)D^{-1/2}\| \geq 2 k n^{1/k}/\sqrt{\Upsilon}] \leq 2^{-k}$.

nodes.name: Trace Bound on $\Delta^k$
nodes.statement: For even $k$: $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{tr}(\Delta^k)] \leq n k^k / \Upsilon^{k/2}$, where $\Delta = D^{-1}(\widetilde{A}-A)$.

nodes.name: Magnitude Bound on $\Delta_{i,j}$
nodes.statement: $|\Delta_{i,j}| \leq 1/\Upsilon$ for every edge $(i,j)$.

nodes.name: Edge Moment Bound $\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{r,t}^k \Delta_{t,r}^l]$
nodes.statement: For all edges $(r,t)$, integers $k\geq 1$, $l\geq 0$: $\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{r,t}^k \Delta_{t,r}^l] \leq \frac{1}{\Upsilon^{k+l-1}} \frac{1}{d_r}$.

nodes.name: Sampled Degrees Concentration
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\|D^{-1/2}(D-\widetilde{D})D^{-1/2}\| \geq \epsilon] \leq 2 n e^{-\Upsilon \epsilon^2/3}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff Bound (Raghavan variant)
nodes.statement: For independent $X_i$ taking $\alpha_i\in[0,\beta]$ with prob. $p_i$ and $0$ otherwise, with $X=\sum X_i$, $\mu=\mathbb{E}[X]$: both $\Pr[X>(1+\epsilon)\mu]$ and $\Pr[X<(1-\epsilon)\mu]$ are at most $(e^\epsilon/(1+\epsilon)^{1+\epsilon})^{\mu/\beta}$, and at most $e^{-\mu\epsilon^2/3\beta}$ for $\epsilon<1$.
conclusions: Same bound for the lower tail; both are $\leq e^{-\mu\epsilon^2/3\beta}$ for $\epsilon<1$

nodes.name: Existence of Spectral Decomposition
nodes.statement: Every graph $G=(V,E)$ has a $(6 \log_{4/3} 2m)^{-1}$-decomposition with $|\partial(A_1,\dots,A_k)| \leq |E|/2$.

nodes.name: Sparsest Cuts as Certificates
nodes.statement: If $S \subset B$ maximizes $\mathrm{vol}(S)$ among sets satisfying $\mathrm{vol}(S)\leq \mathrm{vol}(B)/2$ and $\Phi_B(S)\leq \phi$, and $\mathrm{vol}(S) = \alpha\,\mathrm{vol}(B)$ with $\alpha\leq 1/3$, then $\Phi_{B-S} \geq \phi(1-3\alpha)/(1-\alpha)$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Guarantee
nodes.statement: $D = \approxcut(G,\phi,p)$ satisfies (A.1) $\mathrm{vol}(D) \leq (23/25)\mathrm{vol}(V)$; (A.2) $D \neq \emptyset \Rightarrow \Phi_G(D) \leq \phi$; (A.3) with prob. $\geq 1-p$ either $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/29$ or $\exists W \supseteq V-D$ with $\Phi_W \geq f_2(\phi) = c_2 \phi^2/\log^4 m$. Expected runtime $O(\phi^{-4} m \log^9 m \log(1/p))$.
conclusions: (A.3) with prob. $\geq 1-p$: either $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/29$ or there exists $W \supseteq V-D$ with $\Phi_W \geq c_2 \phi^2 / \log^4 m$

nodes.name: Partition Guarantee
nodes.statement: $D = \partition(G,\tau,p)$ satisfies (P.1) $\mathrm{vol}(D) \leq (7/8)\mathrm{vol}(V)$; (P.2) $D \neq \emptyset \Rightarrow \Phi_G(D) \leq \tau$; (P.3) for every $S$ with $\mathrm{vol}(S)\leq \mathrm{vol}(V)/2$ and $\Phi_G(S) \leq f_1(\tau)= c_1 \tau^2/\log^3 m$, with prob. $\geq 1-p$ either $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/4$ or $\mathrm{vol}(S \cap D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(S)/2$. Runtime $O(\tau^{-4} m \log^7 m \log(1/p))$.

nodes.name: Partition2 Guarantee
nodes.statement: $D = \partitiontwo(G,\theta,p,\epsilon)$ satisfies (Q.1) $\mathrm{vol}(D) \leq (9/10)\mathrm{vol}(V)$; (Q.2) $D \neq \emptyset \Rightarrow \Phi_G(D) \leq \theta$; (Q.3) for every $S$ with $\mathrm{vol}(S)\leq \mathrm{vol}(V)/2$ and $\Phi_G(S) \leq f_1(\theta/9)$, with prob. $\geq 1-p$ either $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/5$ or $\mathrm{vol}(S \cap D) \geq (1-\delta)\mathrm{vol}(S)$ where $\delta = \max(\epsilon, \Phi_G(S)/f_1(\theta/9))$. Runtime $O(\theta^{-4} m \log^7 m \log(1/\epsilon)\log(\log(1/\epsilon)/p))$.

nodes.name: $V_{i+1} \subseteq W_{i+1} \subseteq W_i$
nodes.statement: For all $i$ such that $W_{i+1}$ is defined, $V_{i+1} \subseteq W_{i+1} \subseteq W_i$.
assumptions: Definitions of $V_i$, $W_i$, $S_i$, $U_i$ from the inductive procedure for ApproxCut

nodes.name: $U_i$ Has High Conductance
nodes.statement: For all $i$ such that $U_i$ is defined, $\Phi_{U_i} \geq \theta_i$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Volume Lemma 1 (vol intersection)
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(S_i) \leq (2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ and $\mathrm{vol}(V_{i-1}) \geq (16/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, then $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap (S_{i-1}\cap V_i)) \geq 2\epsilon\,\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Lemma 2 (Geometric Shrinking of $S_i$)
nodes.statement: Under the standing hypotheses, $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap V_{i+1}) \leq \mathrm{vol}(S_{i-1}\cap V_i)/2$ and $\mathrm{vol}(S_i) \leq \mathrm{vol}(S_{i-1})/2$ for $i\geq 1$. In particular, $S_r$ is empty if defined.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Lemma 3 (Lower Bound on $\theta_i$)
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:ac2}, $\theta_i \geq c_2 \phi^2 / \log^4 m$ for some absolute constant $c_2$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Lemma 4 (Conductance of $S_i \cap V_i$)
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(S_i)\leq(2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, $\mathrm{vol}(V_i)\geq(16/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, and $\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)\geq\epsilon\,\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$, then $\Phi_{G\{V_i\}}(S_i\cap V_i) \leq (\epsilon/\delta) f_1(\phi/104)$ where $\delta = \mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)/\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$. If additionally $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap V_{i+1}) \leq (\epsilon/\delta)\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)$, then $\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_{i+1}) \leq \epsilon\,\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$.

nodes.name: Boundary Containment Claim
nodes.statement: $\partial_{V_i}(S_i \cap V_i) \subseteq \partial_{W_i}(S_i)$.
assumptions: $S_i$, $V_i$, $W_i$ from the inductive procedure for ApproxCut

nodes.name: ApproxCut Lemma 5 (Big $S_i$, Small Intersection)
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(V_i)\geq(16/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, $\mathrm{vol}(S_i)\geq(2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, and $\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)\leq \mathrm{vol}(V_i)/2$, then $\Phi_{G\{V_i\}}(S_i\cap V_i) \leq 2\epsilon f_1(\phi/104)$. Moreover if $\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i \cap D_{i+1}) \geq (1-2\epsilon)\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)$, then $\mathrm{vol}(D_{i+1}) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/29$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut Lemma 6 (Big $S_i$, Big Intersection)
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(V_i)\geq(16/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ and $\mathrm{vol}(S_i\cap V_i)\geq \mathrm{vol}(V_i)/2$, then $\Phi_{G\{V_i\}}(S_i\cap V_i) \leq 2\epsilon f_1(\phi/104)$. Moreover if $\mathrm{vol}((V_i-(S_i\cap V_i))\cap D_{i+1}) \geq (1-\epsilon)\mathrm{vol}(V_i-(S_i\cap V_i))$, then $\mathrm{vol}(D_{i+1}) \geq (3/16)\mathrm{vol}(V)$.

nodes.name: PartitionAndSample Guarantee
nodes.statement: (PS.1) $|\partial(V_1,\dots,V_k)| \leq |E|/2$. With prob. $\geq 1-3n\hat{p}$: (PS.2) $G_0 + \sum_{i=1}^k \widetilde{G}_i$ is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)^{1+\log_{29/28}\mathrm{vol}(V)}$-approximation of $G$; (PS.3) total edges in $\widetilde{G}_1,\dots,\widetilde{G}_k$ is at most $c_3 \epsilon^{-2}|V|\log^{30}(n/p)$.
conclusions: With prob. $\geq 1-3n\hat p$: (PS.2) and (PS.3) as stated

nodes.name: UnwtedSparsify Guarantee
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{G} = \unwtedsparsify(G,\epsilon,p)$ satisfies: (U.1) edges of $\widetilde{G}$ are a subset of edges of $G$; with prob. $\geq 1-p$, (U.2) $\widetilde{G}$ is a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $G$, (U.3) $\widetilde{G}$ has at most $c_4 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{31}(n/p)$ edges. Expected runtime $O(m \log(1/p)\log^{15} n)$.

nodes.name: BoundedSparsify Guarantee
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{G} = \boundedsparsify(G,\epsilon,p)$ for $G$ with integral weights and $U-1$ max weight satisfies: (B.1) edge subset; with prob. $\geq 1-p$, (B.2) $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation; (B.3) at most $c_4 \epsilon^{-2} n \log U \log^{31}(n/p)$ edges. Runtime $O(m \log U \log(1/p) \log^{15} n)$.

nodes.name: Pullback Approximation Lemma
nodes.statement: Under the high-weight/low-weight conditions, if $\widetilde{G}_0$ is a pullback of a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of the contraction of $G_0$ and $c\geq 3$, then $\widetilde{G}_0 + G_1$ is an $\alpha$-approximation of $G$ for $\alpha = (1+\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2$.
assumptions: $\widetilde{G}_0$ a pullback of a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of contraction of $G_0$ under $\pi$
(1) each $V_i$ connected by $E_1$; (2) edges in $E_1$ have weight $\geq c^2 n^3$; (3) edges in $E_0$ have weight $1$

nodes.name: Path Preconditions an Edge
nodes.statement: If $(u,v)$ is an edge of weight $1$ and $F$ is a path from $u$ to $v$ with edge weights $w_1,\dots,w_k$, then $(u,v) \preceq (1/w_1+\dotsb+1/w_k) F$.

nodes.name: Bound on Number of Sparsify Clusters
nodes.statement: Let $k_i$ be the number of clusters described by $\sparsify$ at step 4b. Then $\sum_i k_i \leq 2 n l$.

nodes.name: Sparsify Guarantee
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{G} = \sparsify(G,\epsilon,p)$ for weighted $G$ with edge weights $\leq 1$: (X.1) edge subset; with prob. $\geq 1-p$, (X.2) $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation; (X.3) at most $c_5 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{33}(n/p)$ edges. Runtime $O(m \log(1/p) \log^{17} n)$.
assumptions: $G$ weighted on $n$ vertices, max edge weight $\leq 1$

nodes.name: Sparsify Calculation
nodes.statement: If $\beta,\gamma<1/2$ and $\widetilde{G}+\beta\widehat{G}$ is a $(1+\gamma)$-approximation of $(1+\beta)\widehat{G}$, then $\widetilde{G}$ is a $(1+\beta)(1+\gamma)$-approximation of $\widehat{G}$.

nodes.name: Sparsify2 Guarantee
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{G} = \sparsifytwo(G,\epsilon,p)$: (Y.1) edge subset; with prob. $\geq 1-(4/3)p$, (Y.2) $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation; (Y.3) at most $c_6 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{34}(n/p)$ edges; (Y.4) every vertex has blow-up $\leq 2$. Runtime $O(m \log(1/p) \log^{17} n)$.
conclusions: (Y.1)–(Y.4) as stated, including bounded vertex blow-up

nodes.name: Expected Blow-Up
nodes.statement: For $\widetilde{G} = \sparsifytwo(G)$ and every $e \in E$, $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}(e)] \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Maximum Edge Blow-Up
nodes.statement: For $\widetilde{G} = \sparsifytwo(G)$ and every edge $(u,v) \in E$: $\mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}(u,v) \leq \frac{\min(d_u,d_v)}{48 \log(3n/p)^2}$.

nodes.name: Sample
nodes.statement: Edge-sampling routine: include each edge with probability $p_{i,j} = \min(1, \Upsilon/\min(d_i,d_j))$ at re-weighted weight $1/p_{i,j}$.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. $k = \max(\log_2(3/p), \log_2 n)$. 2. $\Upsilon = (12 k/(\epsilon\lambda))^2$. 3. For each edge $(i,j)$ set $p_{i,j} = \min(1, \Upsilon/\min(d_i,d_j))$. 4. With prob. $p_{i,j}$ add edge of weight $1/p_{i,j}$ to $\widetilde{G}$.

nodes.name: idealDecomp
nodes.statement: Recursive (computationally infeasible) procedure that decomposes $G$ by repeatedly carving out a max-volume sparse cut and recursing.
output: Partition of $B$ into parts of conductance $\geq \phi/3$
nodes.pseudocode: 1. If $\Phi_B \geq \phi$ return $B$. 2. Let $S$ be the max-vol set with $\mathrm{vol}(S) \leq \mathrm{vol}(B)/2$ and $\Phi_B(S) \leq \phi$. 3. If $\mathrm{vol}(S) \leq \mathrm{vol}(B)/4$, return $(B-S, \mathtt{idealDecomp}(S,\phi))$. 4. Else return $(\mathtt{idealDecomp}(B-S,\phi), \mathtt{idealDecomp}(S,\phi))$.

nodes.name: ApproxCut
nodes.statement: Iteratively peels off cuts via $\partitiontwo$ until either remaining volume drops below $(4/5)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ or after $r=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil$ rounds.
nodes.pseudocode: 0. $V_0 = V$, $j=0$. 1. $r = \lceil\log_2 m\rceil$, $\epsilon = \min(1/2r, 1/5)$. 2. While $j < r$ and $\mathrm{vol}(V_j) \geq (4/5)\mathrm{vol}(V)$: $j=j+1$; $D_j = \partitiontwo(G\{V_{j-1}\}, (2/23)\phi, p/2r, \epsilon)$; $V_j = V_{j-1} - D_j$. 3. Return $D = D_1 \cup \dotsb \cup D_j$.

nodes.name: Partition2
nodes.statement: Repeats $\partition$ to accumulate cuts until $1/5$ volume is removed or $r$ rounds elapse, strengthening (P.3.b) to remove a $(1-\delta)$ fraction of every low-conductance set.
nodes.pseudocode: 0. $W_0=V$, $j=0$, $r=\lceil\log_2(1/\epsilon)\rceil$. 1. While $j<r$ and $\mathrm{vol}(W_j) \geq (4/5)\mathrm{vol}(V)$: $j=j+1$; $D_j = \partition(G\{W_{j-1}\},\theta/9,p/r)$; $W_j = W_{j-1}-D_j$. 2. Return $D = D_1\cup\dotsb\cup D_j$.

nodes.name: Partition (cited)
nodes.statement: Local-clustering routine that returns a low-conductance cut $D$ with the per-set guarantee (P.3).

nodes.name: PartitionAndSample
nodes.statement: Uses $\approxcut$ to peel off small cuts and applies $\sample$ to high-conductance pieces, recursing on large cuts until the graph is fully decomposed and sampled.
output: Sparsifiers $\widetilde{G}_1,\dots,\widetilde{G}_k$ for the parts of a decomposition of $G$
nodes.pseudocode: 0. $\lambda = f_2(\phi)^2/2$. 1. $D=\approxcut(G,\phi,\hat p)$. 2. If $D=\emptyset$ return $\widetilde{G}_1=\sample(G,\hat\epsilon,\hat p,\lambda)$. 3. Else if $\mathrm{vol}(D)\leq \mathrm{vol}(V)/29$: $\widetilde{G}_1 = \sample(G(V-D),\hat\epsilon,\hat p,\lambda)$; return $(\widetilde{G}_1, \partsample(G(D),\phi,\hat\epsilon,\hat p))$. 4. Else: recurse on $G(V-D)$ and $G(D)$ separately.

nodes.name: UnwtedSparsify
nodes.statement: Top-level nearly-linear-time sparsifier for unweighted graphs: applies $\partsample$, then recursively sparsifies the boundary graph of the resulting decomposition.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. If $\mathrm{vol}(V) \leq c_3 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{30}(n/p)$ return $G$. 2. Set $\phi=(2\log_{29/28}\mathrm{vol}(V))^{-1}$, $\hat p = p/(6n\log_2 n)$, $\hat\epsilon = \epsilon (\ln 2)^2/((1+2\log_{29/28} n)(2\log n))$. 3. $(\widetilde{G}_1,\dots,\widetilde{G}_k) = \partsample(G,\phi,\hat\epsilon,\hat p)$. 4. $G_0$ has edges $\partial(V_1,\dots,V_k)$. 5. $\widetilde{G}_0 = \unwtedsparsify(G_0,\epsilon,p)$. 6. Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_{i=0}^k \widetilde{G}_i$.

nodes.name: BoundedSparsify
nodes.statement: Decomposes a bounded-integer-weight graph into binary layers of weight-$1$ graphs and runs $\unwtedsparsify$ on each.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Decompose $G = \sum_{i=0}^{u-1} 2^i G_i$ with each $G_i$ weight-1. 2. $\widetilde{G}_i = \unwtedsparsify(G_i, \epsilon, p/u)$. 3. Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_i 2^i \widetilde{G}_i$.

nodes.name: Sparsify
nodes.statement: Sparsifies arbitrary-weight graphs by truncating weights to a few significant bits, layering into weight-1 graphs, contracting clusters connected by much heavier edges, and applying $\boundedsparsify$ on each contraction's pullback.
nodes.pseudocode: 0. Set $Q=\lceil 6/\epsilon\rceil$, $b=c=6/\epsilon$, $\hat\epsilon = \epsilon/6$, $l=\lceil\log_2 2 b c^2 n^3\rceil$. 1. For each edge $e$, truncate $w_e$ to $z_e = q_e 2^{-r_e}$ with $Q\leq q_e<2Q$. 2. $\widehat{G} = \sum_{i\geq 0} 2^{-i} G^i$. 3. Compute connected components $D^{\leq i}_j$ under $E^{\leq i}$. 4. For each $i$ with $E^i\neq\emptyset$: form clusters $C^i_j = D^{\leq i-l}_j \cap V^i$, contract under $\pi$ to get $H^i$, set $\widetilde{H}^i = \boundedsparsify(H^i,\hat\epsilon, p/(2nl))$, take pullback $\widetilde{G}^i$. 5. Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_i 2^{-i} \widetilde{G}^i$.

nodes.name: Sparsify2
nodes.statement: Modifies $\sparsify$ by sub-dividing clusters by degree class and using random pullbacks so that every vertex in the output has bounded blow-up.
nodes.pseudocode: Replace steps 4a–4e of $\sparsify$: 4a. For each $\delta$ let $V_\delta$ be the vertices of degree in $[2^\delta, 2^{\delta+1})$. 4b. For each $\delta$, intersect $V_\delta$ with the components $D^{\leq i-l}_j \cap V^i$, and sub-divide any cluster with boundary $> 2^{\delta+2}$ into sub-clusters with boundary in $[2^\delta, 2^{\delta+2}]$. 4c. Contract under the resulting partition. 4e. Sparsify the contraction with $\boundedsparsify(\cdot, \hat\epsilon, p/(c_8 n l \log n))$ and take a uniformly random pullback of each chosen edge.

nodes.name: Complete Graph Sparsifier
nodes.statement: A weighted Ramanujan graph (each edge $\times n/d$) is a $(1 - 2\sqrt{d-1}/d)^{-1}$-spectral approximation of the complete graph $K_n$.

nodes.name: Joined Complete Graphs
nodes.statement: For two $K_n$'s joined by a single edge $e$, the sparsifier is $e + (n/d)\cdot$(Ramanujan on each side); the bridge edge $e$ must be kept exactly while interior edges may be sparsified.

nodes.name: Cut vs Spectral Sparsification Distinction
nodes.statement: A ring of $n$ size-$k$ vertex sets connected by complete bipartite graphs plus one diametral edge $e$ is a $(1+1/2k)$-cut-approximation but not a $\sigma$-spectral-approximation for any $\sigma < 1 + n/4k^2$.

nodes.name: Sampling Probability $p_{i,j}$
nodes.statement: $p_{i,j} = \min\!\left(1, \frac{\Upsilon}{\min(d_i,d_j)}\right)$ for all edges $(i,j)$.

nodes.name: $f_1$ and $f_2$ Conductance Functions
nodes.statement: $f_1(\tau) = c_1 \tau^2/\log^3 m$ and $f_2(\phi) = c_2 \phi^2/\log^4 m$ for absolute constants $c_1, c_2$.

nodes.name: Sparsification Improvements (Final Remarks)
nodes.statement: Subsequent work (Spielman \& Srivastava; Batson, Spielman \& Srivastava; Koutis, Miller, Peng; Andersen \& Peres) yields $O(n\log n/\epsilon^2)$ and ultimately $O(n/\epsilon^2)$ sparsifiers and faster Laplacian solvers that no longer rely on the construction of the present paper.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma normSmallApprox
nodes.statement: Project $y = D^{1/2} x$ orthogonal to $D^{1/2}\mathbf{1}$, bound $x^T \widetilde{L} x$ by $(\lambda \pm \epsilon)/\lambda \cdot x^T L x$ using the operator-norm hypothesis.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma sampling (norm bound)
nodes.statement: Switch to $\Delta = D^{-1}(\widetilde{A}-A)$, bound an even moment of its eigenvalues by $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{tr}(\Delta^k)]$ from Lemma trace, and apply Markov's inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma trace
nodes.statement: Encode walks contributing to $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{tr}(\Delta^k)]$ by triples $(T,\tau,\sigma)$ with $|T|\leq k/2$, bound moments using Lemma edgeExpec, and count valid encodings via a random-walk-generation argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim magnitude
nodes.statement: Case-split on whether $p_{i,j}=1$ or $p_{i,j}<1$; bound $|\Delta_{i,j}|$ by $1/\min(d_i,d_j) \leq 1/\Upsilon$ using $p_{i,j} = \Upsilon/\min(d_i,d_j)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma edgeExpec
nodes.statement: Reduce by Claim magnitude to $k+l=2$, then directly compute $\mathbb{E}[(\widetilde{A}_{r,t}-1)^2] = (1-p_{r,t})/p_{r,t}$ and substitute $p_{r,t}=\Upsilon/\min(d_r,d_t)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma sampledDegrees
nodes.statement: Each $\widetilde{d}_i$ is a sum of independent $0$/$\leq d_i/\Upsilon$ variables with mean $d_i$; apply the Chernoff variant from Theorem chernoff and a union bound over $i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem sampling
nodes.statement: Split $L - \widetilde{L}$ into the off-diagonal part $A - \widetilde{A}$ and the diagonal part $D - \widetilde{D}$; bound each in operator norm via Lemmas sampling and sampledDegrees, then conclude via Lemma normSmallApprox; bound $|\widetilde{F}|$ by Chernoff.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma certificate
nodes.statement: Suppose for contradiction that $\Phi_{B-S} < \phi\beta$ with $\beta = (1-3\alpha)/(1-\alpha)$. Set $T = R \cup S$ and case-split on $\mathrm{vol}(T) \lessgtr \mathrm{vol}(B)/2$ to derive a larger sparse cut, contradicting maximality of $S$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem graphDecompExist
nodes.statement: Apply $\mathtt{idealDecomp}(V,\phi)$ with $\phi = (2\log_{4/3}\mathrm{vol}(V))^{-1}$; Lemma certificate yields $\Phi_{A_i} \geq \phi/3$, and the recursion depth is at most $\log_{4/3}\mathrm{vol}(V)$, so the boundary has at most $|E|\phi\log_{4/3}\mathrm{vol}(V) \leq |E|/2$ edges.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma partition2
nodes.statement: Bound $\mathrm{vol}(D)$ via geometric accumulation of cuts; bound $\Phi_G(D)$ from (P.2) for each piece; for (Q.3), iteratively show $S_j$ satisfies condition (P.3) in $G\{W_j\}$ so that $\partition$ failing for some $j$ has probability $\leq r(p/r)=p$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem ApproxCut
nodes.statement: Maintain inductive sets $S_i \subseteq W_i$ via Lemmas ac1–ac6: if any $\mathrm{vol}(S_i) \geq (2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, conclude (A.3.a); otherwise iterate Lemma ac4 to get $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap V_{i+1}) \leq \epsilon\,\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$, then Lemma ac2 forces $S_r=\emptyset$ so $W_i = U_i$ has high conductance by Claim uiExpander and Lemma ac3.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma partsample
nodes.statement: Recursion depth is $\leq \log_{29/28}\mathrm{vol}(V)$. Assume the success of all calls to $\sample$ and $\approxcut$ (probability $\geq 1-3n\hat p$ via union bound); use induction on depth to show $\sum \widetilde{G}_i + \partial$ is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)^{d+1}$-approximation of $G$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma unwtsparsify
nodes.statement: Recursion depth is $\leq 2\log n$, so by union bound (PS.2), (PS.3) hold throughout with prob. $\geq 1-p$; induct on depth using $(1+x\ln 2/k)^k \leq 1+x$ to get $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation overall.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma boundedsparsify
nodes.statement: Each $\widetilde{G}_i$ is a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $G_i$ by Lemma unwtsparsify; summing $\sum 2^i \widetilde{G}_i$ preserves the approximation factor for $G = \sum 2^i G_i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma Path
nodes.statement: Set $y(i) = \sqrt{w_i}(x_i - x_{i-1})$ and apply Cauchy–Schwarz to $\sum (1/\sqrt{w_i})\cdot y(i)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma pullback
nodes.statement: Pick representatives $v_i \in V_i$, define $I = F + G_1$, $\widetilde{I} = \widetilde{F} + G_1$. Show (a) $I$ is a $(1+1/c)$-approximation of $G$ via Lemma Path applied to each cross-cluster edge, (b) $\widetilde{I}$ is a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $I$ from contraction approximation, (c) $\widetilde{I}$ is a $(1+1/c)$-approximation of $\widetilde{G}_0 + G_1$ symmetrically.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma sparsifyNumClusters
nodes.statement: Each cluster $C^i_j$ has $\geq 1$ edge of $E^i$ leaving it, so $\eta_i \leq \eta_{i-l} - k_i/2$. Since $\eta_i \geq 0$ and $\eta_0 \leq n$, summing yields $\sum_i k_i \leq 2 n l$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem sparsify
nodes.statement: Truncate weights to get $\widehat{G}$ with $\widehat{G} \preceq G \preceq (1+1/Q)\widehat{G}$. Apply Lemma pullback per layer and Proposition sparsifyCalc to convert the $(1+\hat\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2$-approximation of $(1+\beta)\widehat{G}$ into a $(1+\hat\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2(1+\beta)$-approximation of $\widehat{G}$, hence of $G$ within $(1+\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition sparsifyCalc
nodes.statement: From $\widetilde{G}+\beta\widehat{G} \preceq (1+\gamma)(1+\beta)\widehat{G}$ derive $\widetilde{G}\preceq(1+\beta)(1+\gamma)\widehat{G}$; the reverse inequality follows by manipulating $(1+\beta)\widehat{G} \preceq (1+\gamma)(\widetilde{G}+\beta\widehat{G})$ under $\beta,\gamma<1/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem sparsifytwo
nodes.statement: Bound $\sum_{i,\delta} t^\delta_i \leq c_8 n l \log n$ via the boundary-volume argument (4a–4b), then apply the same edge-count and approximation analysis as in Theorem sparsify; conclude (Y.4) by combining Lemma expectedBlowUp and Lemma maxBlowUp with the negative-association Chernoff bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma expectedBlowUp
nodes.statement: Verify $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{blowup}_{\widetilde{G}}(e)] = 1$ for $\sample$, then propagate the identity through $\unwtedsparsify$ (edge-disjoint partition + sample), $\boundedsparsify$ (linear combination), and $\sparsifytwo$ (random pullback yields $1/w_e$ correction balancing $w_e$).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma maxBlowUp
nodes.statement: Show $\sample$ produces blow-up $\leq \min(d_u,d_v)/(16\log(3/p))^2$; propagate through $\unwtedsparsify$ and $\boundedsparsify$; for $\sparsifytwo$ use $d_v \geq 4 d_a$ in $H^i$ and sum $2^{-i}/z_{u,v}$ to get the stated bound.

nodes.name: Encode each walk by $(T,\tau,\sigma)$
nodes.statement: Identify every $(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})$ contributing to $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{tr}(\Delta^k)]$ with a closed walk on $A$, then code it by the set $T$ of fresh-edge time steps, the map $\tau$ from repeated steps to their first occurrence, and $\sigma:T\to[n]$ assigning vertices.

nodes.name: Show $|T| \leq k/2$ for non-zero walks
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{v_i,v_j}] = 0$, every edge in the walk must appear at least twice for the term to be non-zero, forcing $|T| \leq k/2$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma edgeExpec to bound the per-$T$ moment
nodes.statement: By Lemma edgeExpec, the inner expectation per $s\in T$ is bounded by $1/\Upsilon^{|\{i:\tau(i)=s\}|} \cdot 1/d_{v_{s-1}}$, giving a $1/\Upsilon^{k-|T|}$ factor when multiplied across $T$.

nodes.name: Bound the $\sigma$-sum by a random-walk argument
nodes.statement: Sample $\sigma(s)$ as a random neighbor of $v_{s-1}$; the success probability of generating any particular valid $\sigma$ is $\prod_{s\in T} 1/d_{v_{s-1}}$, so $\sum_\sigma \prod_{s\in T} 1/d_{v_{s-1}} \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Combine to bound diagonal entry of $\mathbb{E}[\Delta^k]$
nodes.statement: There are $\leq 2^k$ choices for $T$ and $\leq |T|^k$ for $\tau$; combining with the inner bound and $|T|\leq k/2$ gives $\mathbb{E}[(\Delta^k)_{v_0,v_k}] \leq k^k/\Upsilon^{k/2}$. Summing over $v_0=v_k$ proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Setup: split $L-\widetilde{L}$ into adjacency and degree parts
nodes.statement: Since $L$ and $\widetilde{L}$ differ only on rows/columns of $S$, restrict to $L(S)$ and bound $\|D(S)^{-1/2}(L(S)-\widetilde{L}(S))D(S)^{-1/2}\|$ by $\|A(S)-\widetilde{A}(S)\|$ + $\|D(S)-\widetilde{D}(S)\|$ in normalized form.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma sampling to the adjacency term
nodes.statement: Choose $k$ so $2 k n^{1/k}/\sqrt{\Upsilon} \leq \epsilon\lambda/3$; Lemma sampling yields $\Pr[\text{adjacency term} \geq \epsilon\lambda/3] \leq p/3$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma sampledDegrees to the degree term
nodes.statement: Lemma sampledDegrees with $\epsilon\lambda/3$ gives $\Pr[\text{degree term} \geq \epsilon\lambda/3] \leq 2 n e^{-\Upsilon(\epsilon\lambda/3)^2/3} \leq p/3$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma normSmallApprox to conclude approximation
nodes.statement: With prob. $\geq 1-2p/3$, $\|D^{-1/2}(L-\widetilde{L})D^{-1/2}\| \leq 2\epsilon\lambda/3$; Lemma normSmallApprox then gives $\widetilde{G}$ a $\sigma$-approximation with $\sigma = \lambda/(\lambda - 2\epsilon\lambda/3) \leq 1+\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem chernoff to bound $|\widetilde{F}|$
nodes.statement: Indicator sum has $\mathbb{E}[\sum X_{(i,j)}] \leq \Upsilon|S|$; Chernoff with $\epsilon=1$ gives $\Pr[\sum X_{(i,j)} \geq 2\Upsilon|S|] \leq p/3$.

nodes.name: Setup contradiction: assume $\Phi_{B-S} < \phi\beta$
nodes.statement: Set $\beta = (1-3\alpha)/(1-\alpha)$ and assume by contradiction there exists $R \subset B-S$ with $\Phi_{B-S}(R) < \phi\beta$ and $\mathrm{vol}(R) \leq \mathrm{vol}(B-S)/2$.

nodes.name: Bound boundary of $T = R \cup S$
nodes.statement: $|E(T,B-T)| \leq |E(S,B-S)| + |E(R,B-S-R)| < \phi\,\mathrm{vol}(S) + (\phi\beta)\,\mathrm{vol}(R)$.

nodes.name: Case $\mathrm{vol}(T) \leq \mathrm{vol}(B)/2$
nodes.statement: Then $\mathrm{vol}(T) > \mathrm{vol}(S)$ and $\Phi_B(T) < \phi$, contradicting maximality of $S$.

nodes.name: Case $\mathrm{vol}(T) > \mathrm{vol}(B)/2$
nodes.statement: Show $\mathrm{vol}(B-T) > (1-\alpha)/2 \cdot \mathrm{vol}(B) > \mathrm{vol}(S)$ and $\Phi_B(T) \leq \phi$ via the choice of $\beta$, again contradicting the maximality of $S$.

nodes.name: Set up sets $W_i, U_i, S_i$ inductively
nodes.statement: Set $W_0 = V_0 = V$, $\sigma_0 = \epsilon f_1(\phi/104)$. Iteratively define $S_i$ as the max-volume set in $W_i$ of conductance $\leq \sigma_i$, $U_i = W_i - S_i$, $\theta_i = (1-3\mathrm{vol}(S_i)/\mathrm{vol}(W_i))\sigma_i$, $\sigma_{i+1} = (1-2\epsilon)\theta_i$, $W_{i+1} = U_i \cup (S_i \cap V_{i+1})$.

nodes.name: Case-split on whether $V_i$ shrinks too much
nodes.statement: If some $\mathrm{vol}(V_i) < (16/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ then $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/17$ and (A.3.a) holds.

nodes.name: Big $S_i$ case via Lemmas ac5/ac6
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(S_i) \geq (2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$, by Lemmas ac5/ac6 either $S_i \cap V_i$ or $V_i - (S_i \cap V_i)$ satisfies the Q3 conditions in $G\{V_i\}$, so success of $\partitiontwo$ gives $\mathrm{vol}(D) \geq \mathrm{vol}(V)/29$ — establishing (A.3.a).

nodes.name: Small $S_i$ case via Lemma ac4
nodes.statement: Otherwise $\mathrm{vol}(S_i) \leq (2/17)\mathrm{vol}(V)$; if $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap V_i)$ is large enough Lemma ac4 + success of $\partitiontwo$ gives $\mathrm{vol}(S_i \cap V_{i+1}) \leq \epsilon\,\mathrm{vol}(S_i)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma ac2 to vanish $S_r$
nodes.statement: Lemma ac2 yields $S_r = \emptyset$ if defined, so some $W_i = U_i$ has high conductance by Claim uiExpander combined with the $\theta_i \geq c_2\phi^2/\log^4 m$ bound from Lemma ac3 — establishing (A.3.b) for $W = W_i \supseteq V - D$.

nodes.name: Bound recursion depth of partsample
nodes.statement: Each recursive call has volume $\leq (28/29)\,\mathrm{vol}(V)$, so recursion depth is at most $\log_{29/28}\mathrm{vol}(V)$, immediately yielding (PS.1).

nodes.name: Set up high-probability assumptions on Sample/ApproxCut calls
nodes.statement: Assume that every $\sample$ output is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)$-approximation with the (S.2) edge bound, and that every small-$D$ $\approxcut$ admits a witness $W \supseteq V-D$ of conductance $\geq f_2(\phi)$. Union bounds over $\leq n$ calls show all assumptions hold w.p. $\geq 1-3n\hat p$.

nodes.name: Inductive base: no recursion
nodes.statement: If $\partsample$ does not call itself it returns the output of $\sample$ in line 2, which is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)$-approximation by assumption 1.

nodes.name: Inductive step: small $D$ case
nodes.statement: When $\mathrm{vol}(D) \leq (1/29)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ recurse on $H = G(D)$, apply assumption 2 to $\widetilde{G}_1$ and the inductive hypothesis $H_0 + \sum \widetilde{H}_i \preceq (1+\hat\epsilon)^d H$, and combine via $G = G(V-D) + H + \partial(V-D,D)$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: big $D$ case
nodes.statement: When $\mathrm{vol}(D) > (1/29)\mathrm{vol}(V)$ recurse on both $G(D)$ and $G(V-D)$ and add the resulting $(1+\hat\epsilon)^d$-approximations of $H$ and $I$ to obtain a $(1+\hat\epsilon)^d$-approximation of $G$.

nodes.name: Bound the recursion depth
nodes.statement: From (PS.1) applied to $\unwtedsparsify$, recursion depth $d \leq 2\log n$, so $1 - (2\log n)\cdot 3 n \hat p = 1-p$ probability that (PS.2) and (PS.3) hold throughout.

nodes.name: Inductive proof of approximation factor
nodes.statement: Inductively show $\widetilde{G}$ is a $(1+\epsilon\ln 2/(2\log n + 1))^d$-approximation of $G$ at depth $d$, using $(1+\hat\epsilon)^{1+\log_{29/28} n^2} \leq 1 + \epsilon\ln 2/(2\log n)$ at each step.

nodes.name: Conclude $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation
nodes.statement: Use $(1+\epsilon\ln 2/(2\log n))^{2\log n} \leq 1+\epsilon$ for $\epsilon < 1$ to absorb the depth-$d$ exponent into the final $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation.

nodes.name: Approximate inter-cluster edges via paths in $G_1$
nodes.statement: For each edge $(a,b) \in E_0$, build a path through $\frac{1}{c n^2} G_1$ from $a$ to $v_{\pi(a)}$ and $b$ to $v_{\pi(b)}$ using high-weight edges in $E_1$; Lemma Path then gives $(a,b) \preceq (1+1/c)(f + \frac{1}{c n^2}G_1)$ and the reverse direction.

nodes.name: Sum to relate $G_0 + G_1$ and $F + G_1$
nodes.statement: Sum over the $\leq n^2/2$ edges of $E_0$ to obtain $G_0 \preceq (1+1/c)(F + G_1/(2c))$, then add $G_1$ to both sides to get part (a): $G \preceq (1+1/c)(F + G_1)$.

nodes.name: Approximation $\widetilde{F}$ vs. $F$
nodes.statement: Since $\widetilde{F}$ is a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation of $F$, the sums $\widetilde{I} = \widetilde{F} + G_1$ and $I = F + G_1$ also satisfy the $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation, giving part (b).

nodes.name: Symmetric path argument for $\widetilde{G}_0 + G_1$
nodes.statement: Repeat the path argument from each $\widetilde{G}_0$-edge $(a,b)$ of weight $w$ to its corresponding $\widetilde{F}$-edge of the same weight, summing to obtain part (c): $\widetilde{I}$ is a $(1+1/c)$-approximation of $\widetilde{G}_0 + G_1$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\alpha$-approximation
nodes.statement: Composing parts (a)–(c) gives $\widetilde{G}_0 + G_1$ is an $\alpha$-approximation of $G$ for $\alpha = (1+\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2$.

nodes.name: Truncate weights to $\widehat{G}$
nodes.statement: Set $z_e = q_e 2^{-r_e}$ with $Q\leq q_e<2Q$; conclude $\widehat{G} \preceq G \preceq (1+1/Q)\widehat{G}$.

nodes.name: Bound number of $\boundedsparsify$ calls
nodes.statement: Lemma sparsifyNumClusters bounds the number of layers needing $\boundedsparsify$ by $nl$; union bound yields properties (B.2)/(B.3) for all calls with prob. $\geq 1-p$.

nodes.name: Bound edge count via $\sum_i k_i \leq 2 n l$
nodes.statement: Using (B.3), each $|\widetilde{H}^i| \leq c_4 \hat\epsilon^{-2} k_i \log^{32}(n^2 l/p)$; sum and apply Lemma sparsifyNumClusters to get (X.3): at most $c_5 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{33}(n/p)$ edges.

nodes.name: Sum pullback approximations across layers
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma pullback to each $G^i$ + $c^2 n^3 F^{i-l}$ pair, sum with weights $2^{-i}$ to get that $\widetilde{G} + 2 c^2 n^3 2^{-l} \widehat{G}$ is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2$-approximation of $(1+\beta)\widehat{G}$ with $\beta = 2 c^2 n^3 2^{-l} \leq 1/b$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition sparsifyCalc and finish
nodes.statement: By Proposition sparsifyCalc, $\widetilde{G}$ is a $(1+\hat\epsilon)(1+1/c)^2(1+\beta)$-approximation of $\widehat{G}$, hence of $G$ within $(1+1/Q)$, all bounded by $(1+\epsilon/6)^5 \leq 1+\epsilon$ — establishing (X.2).

nodes.name: Set $k$, $\Upsilon$
nodes.statement: $k = \max(\log_2(3/p), \log_2 n)$; $\Upsilon = (12 k/(\epsilon\lambda))^2$.

nodes.name: Compute per-edge probabilities
nodes.statement: For every edge $(i,j)$ in $G$ set $p_{i,j} = \min(1, \Upsilon/\min(d_i,d_j))$.

nodes.name: Sample edges with re-weighting
nodes.statement: For every edge $(i,j)$ in $G$, with probability $p_{i,j}$ insert an edge of weight $1/p_{i,j}$ between $i$ and $j$ in $\widetilde{G}$.

nodes.name: Test base case
nodes.statement: If $\Phi_B \geq \phi$ then return $B$; else proceed.

nodes.name: Find max-volume sparse cut $S$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be the max-volume subset of $B$ satisfying $\mathrm{vol}(S)\leq\mathrm{vol}(B)/2$ and $\Phi_B(S) \leq \phi$ (NP-hard sub-problem).

nodes.name: Branch on size of $S$
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(S) \leq \mathrm{vol}(B)/4$, return $(B-S, \mathtt{idealDecomp}(S,\phi))$; else return $(\mathtt{idealDecomp}(B-S,\phi), \mathtt{idealDecomp}(S,\phi))$.

nodes.name: Initialize $V_0$, $j$, $r$, $\epsilon$
nodes.statement: Set $V_0 = V$, $j = 0$, $r = \lceil\log_2 m\rceil$, $\epsilon = \min(1/2r, 1/5)$.

nodes.name: Iteratively peel cuts with Partition2
nodes.statement: While $j<r$ and $\mathrm{vol}(V_j) \geq (4/5)\mathrm{vol}(V)$: $j=j+1$; $D_j = \partitiontwo(G\{V_{j-1}\}, (2/23)\phi, p/2r, \epsilon)$; $V_j = V_{j-1}-D_j$.

nodes.name: Return cumulative cut
nodes.statement: Return $D = D_1 \cup \dotsb \cup D_j$.

nodes.name: Initialize state
nodes.statement: Set $W_0=V$, $j=0$, $r = \lceil\log_2(1/\epsilon)\rceil$.

nodes.name: Iteratively call Partition
nodes.statement: While $j<r$ and $\mathrm{vol}(W_j) \geq (4/5)\mathrm{vol}(V)$: $j=j+1$; $D_j = \partition(G\{W_{j-1}\}, \theta/9, p/r)$; $W_j = W_{j-1}-D_j$.

nodes.name: Return cumulative cut
nodes.statement: Return $D = D_1 \cup \dotsb \cup D_j$.

nodes.name: Set $\lambda$ for sampling
nodes.statement: Set $\lambda = f_2(\phi)^2/2$.

nodes.name: Run ApproxCut
nodes.statement: $D = \approxcut(G, \phi, \hat p)$.

nodes.name: Branch on cut size
nodes.statement: If $D = \emptyset$ return $\widetilde{G}_1 = \sample(G, \hat\epsilon, \hat p, \lambda)$. Else if $\mathrm{vol}(D) \leq (1/29)\mathrm{vol}(V)$: $\widetilde{G}_1 = \sample(G(V-D), \hat\epsilon, \hat p, \lambda)$ then recurse on $G(D)$. Else recurse on both $G(V-D)$ and $G(D)$.

nodes.name: Return concatenation
nodes.statement: Return the tuple of $\widetilde{G}_i$ produced from the appropriate branch.

nodes.name: Base case: small graph
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{vol}(V) \leq c_3 \epsilon^{-2} n \log^{30}(n/p)$, return $G$ unchanged.

nodes.name: Set $\phi$, $\hat p$, $\hat\epsilon$
nodes.statement: $\phi = (2 \log_{29/28}\mathrm{vol}(V))^{-1}$, $\hat p = p/(6 n \log_2 n)$, $\hat\epsilon = \epsilon (\ln 2)^2/((1+2\log_{29/28} n)(2\log n))$.

nodes.name: Decompose & sparsify with PartitionAndSample
nodes.statement: $(\widetilde{G}_1,\dots,\widetilde{G}_k) = \partsample(G, \phi, \hat\epsilon, \hat p)$.

nodes.name: Recursively sparsify boundary $G_0$
nodes.statement: Form $G_0$ on $V$ with edges $\partial(V_1,\dots,V_k)$ and set $\widetilde{G}_0 = \unwtedsparsify(G_0, \epsilon, p)$.

nodes.name: Sum sparsifiers
nodes.statement: Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_{i=0}^k \widetilde{G}_i$.

nodes.name: Decompose $G$ into binary layers
nodes.statement: Decompose $G = \sum_{i=0}^{u-1} 2^i G_i$ with each $G_i$ a weight-1 graph (one bit of each edge weight).

nodes.name: Sparsify each layer
nodes.statement: For each $i$ set $\widetilde{G}_i = \unwtedsparsify(G_i, \epsilon, p/u)$.

nodes.name: Combine layers
nodes.statement: Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_i 2^i \widetilde{G}_i$.

nodes.name: Initialize parameters
nodes.statement: Set $Q=\lceil 6/\epsilon\rceil$, $b=c=6/\epsilon$, $\hat\epsilon=\epsilon/6$, $l=\lceil\log_2 2bc^2 n^3\rceil$.

nodes.name: Truncate edge weights
nodes.statement: For each edge $e \in E$, set $r_e$ so $Q \leq 2^{r_e} w_e < 2 Q$, $q_e$ the largest integer with $q_e 2^{-r_e} \leq w_e$, and $z_e = q_e 2^{-r_e}$.

nodes.name: Form $\widehat{G}$ and binary layers $G^i$
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{G} = (V,E,z) = \sum_{i\geq 0} 2^{-i} G^i$ with each $G^i$ weight-1; each edge appears in $\leq \lceil\log_2 2 Q\rceil$ of these layers.

nodes.name: Compute connected components $D^{\leq i}_j$
nodes.statement: For each $i$, let $D^{\leq i}_1, \dots, D^{\leq i}_{\eta_i}$ be the connected components of $V$ under $E^{\leq i} = \bigcup_{j\leq i} E^j$.

nodes.name: Per-layer contraction & sparsification
nodes.statement: For each $i$ with $E^i \neq \emptyset$: form clusters $C^i_j = D^{\leq i-l}_j \cap V^i$ with non-trivial boundary; let $\pi$ be the cluster map; let $H^i$ be the contraction of $(W^i, E^i)$ under $\pi$; set $\widetilde{H}^i = \boundedsparsify(H^i, \hat\epsilon, p/(2nl))$; pull back to get $\widetilde{G}^i$.

nodes.name: Combine layer sparsifiers
nodes.statement: Return $\widetilde{G} = \sum_i 2^{-i} \widetilde{G}^i$.

nodes.name: Sub-divide clusters by degree class
nodes.statement: For each $\delta$, intersect $V_\delta$ (vertices of degree in $[2^\delta, 2^{\delta+1})$) with the components $D^{\leq i-l}_j \cap V^i$; greedily sub-divide every cluster whose boundary in $E^i$ exceeds $2^{\delta+2}$ until each part has boundary in $[2^\delta, 2^{\delta+2}]$.

nodes.name: Contract under refined partition
nodes.statement: Let $\pi$ be the map of the refined partition $\{C^{i,\delta}_j\}_{j,\delta}$ on $W^i$ and let $H^i$ be the contraction of $(W^i, E^i)$ under $\pi$.

nodes.name: Random-pullback sparsification
nodes.statement: Set $\widetilde{H}^i = \boundedsparsify(H^i, \hat\epsilon, p/(c_8 n l \log n))$ and let $\widetilde{G}^i$ be a uniformly random pullback of each chosen edge from $\widetilde{H}^i$ into $E^i$.
